```{ojs}
//| label: ts
//| classes: iihrn-figure

d3regression = require("d3-regression@1.3.10")

hist_path = `${bucket_processed}historical_${stationId}.txt`
historical = FA(hist_path).csv({typed: true})

plotCaption = "© isithotrightnow.com"

// same domain/range Plot's own colour scale below will build, so breakpoints
// line up exactly with the dots' colours. answerColors is 20 equal-sized
// (5%-wide) buckets, so the first/last breakpoints ARE the 5th/95th percentiles.
tavgQuantileScale = d3.scaleQuantile()
  .domain(historical.map(d => d.Tavg))
  .range(answerColors)

tavgBreaks = tavgQuantileScale.quantiles()
tavg05 = tavgBreaks[0]
tavg95 = tavgBreaks[tavgBreaks.length - 1]


// date formatting
today = ({
  Date: new Date(Math.max(
    new Date(statsPlace.isit_maximum_dt),
    new Date(statsPlace.isit_minimum_dt))),
  Tavg: statsPlace.isit_current
})

dayMonthOptions = ({
  month: 'long',
  day: 'numeric'
})

dayMonthLabel = today.Date.toLocaleDateString("en-AU", dayMonthOptions)

// fit against the raw timestamp; .a (the slope) is in °C/ms, used below for
// the trend label. Map the two fitted endpoints back to Date objects so
// Plot.line reads them on the same time x-scale as the dots
tavgFit = d3regression.regressionLinear()
  .x(d => d.Date.getTime())
  .y(d => d.Tavg)
  (historical)
tavgTrend = tavgFit.map(([x, y]) => ({ Date: new Date(x), Tavg: y }))
tavgTrendPerCentury = tavgFit.a * 1000 * 60 * 60 * 24 * 365.25 * 100

leftmostDate = d3.min(historical, d => d.Date)

Plot.plot({
  marks: [
    // historical data
    Plot.dot(historical, {
      x: "Date",
      y: "Tavg",
      fill: "Tavg",
      tip: true,
      r: 2
    }),
    // extreme percentiles
    Plot.ruleY([tavg05, tavg95], {
      stroke: "#333333",
      strokeDasharray: "4,2"
    }),
    Plot.text([
      { y: tavg05, text: `5th percentile: ${tavg05.toFixed(1)}°C` },
      { y: tavg95, text: `95th percentile: ${tavg95.toFixed(1)}°C` }
    ], {
      x: leftmostDate,
      y: "y",
      text: "text",
      textAnchor: "start",
      dy: -15,
      dx: 10,
      fill: "#3333333",
      stroke: "#eeeeee",
      strokeWidth: 5,
    }),
    // trend
    Plot.line(tavgTrend, {
      x: "Date",
      y: "Tavg",
      stroke: "black",
      strokeWidth: 2
    }),
    Plot.text(
      [
        { text: `Trend: ${tavgTrendPerCentury >= 0 ? "+" : ""}${tavgTrendPerCentury.toFixed(1)}°C/century` }
      ], {
      x: tavgTrend[0].Date,
      y: tavgTrend[0].Tavg,
      text: "text",
      textAnchor: "start",
      dy: -21,
      dx: 10,
      fill: "#3333333",
      stroke: "#eeeeee",
      strokeWidth: 5,
    }),
    // today
    Plot.dot([today], {
      x: "Date",
      y: "Tavg",
      fill: tavgQuantileScale(today.Tavg),
      stroke: "#333333",
      r: 6,
    }),
    Plot.text([today], {
      x: "Date",
      y: "Tavg",
      text: () => "TODAY",
      fill: "#333333",
      stroke: "#eeeeee",
      strokeWidth: 5,
      dy: -20
    }),
    Plot.text([today], {
      x: "Date",
      y: "Tavg",
      text: d => `${d.Tavg.toFixed(1)}°C`,
      fill: "#333333",
      stroke: "#eeeeee",
      strokeWidth: 3,
      dy: 20
    }),
    // plot frame
    Plot.frame({
      stroke: "#333333",
      strokeWidth: 3,
      anchor: "bottom"
    }),
    Plot.frame({
      stroke: "#333333",
      strokeWidth: 3,
      anchor: "left"
    })
  ],
  color: {
    type: "quantile",
    range: answerColors
  },
  style: {
    fontFamily: "Roboto Condensed",
    fontWeight: "bold",
    fontSize: 14
  },
  title: `${statsPlace.isit_label} daily average temperatures for the two weeks around ${dayMonthLabel}`,
  caption: plotCaption
})
```

This is the distribution of temperatures typical for this time of year, which we've defined as a seven day window either side of today. Just like a bell curve, the plot is higher at more common temperatures and lower at rare temperatures.

:::

:::{.g-col-12 .g-col-md-8}
```{ojs}
//| label: dist
//| classes: iihrn-figure
//| echo: false

// reproduction of R's stats::density() and stats::bw.nrd0()
gaussianKernel = u => Math.exp(-0.5 * u * u) / Math.sqrt(2 * Math.PI)

// port of R's bw.nrd0(): d3.quantile() uses the same R-7 interpolation as
// R's default quantile(), and d3.deviation() is the same sample sd as R's sd()
bwNrd0 = function(x) {
  const n = x.length
  const hi = d3.deviation(x)
  const iqr = (d3.quantile(x, 0.75) - d3.quantile(x, 0.25)) / 1.34
  let lo = Math.min(hi, iqr)
  if (lo === 0) lo = hi !== 0 ? hi : (Math.abs(x[0]) !== 0 ? Math.abs(x[0]) : 1)
  return 0.9 * lo * Math.pow(n, -0.2)
}

kde = function(bandwidth, grid, data) {
  const n = data.length
  return grid.map(x => [
    x,
    d3.sum(data, d => gaussianKernel((x - d) / bandwidth)) / (n * bandwidth)
  ])
}

historical_tavg = historical.map(d => d.Tavg)
bandwidth = bwNrd0(historical_tavg)

// from/to are passed explicitly in the lambda's stat_density_ridges() call as
// the data's min/max (rather than stats::density()'s default of extending
// 3 bandwidths past each end), and n (grid points) is left at its default of 512
gridFrom = d3.min(historical_tavg)
gridTo = d3.max(historical_tavg)
grid = d3.range(512).map(i => gridFrom + (gridTo - gridFrom) * i / 511)

historical_density = kde(bandwidth, grid, historical_tavg)

// tavg05/tavg95 come from the ts block's tavgQuantileScale (same breaks as
// the colour bands here); tavg50 is the plain median of the same data
tavg50 = d3.median(historical_tavg)

Plot.plot({
  marks: [
    Plot.areaY(historical_density, {
      x: d => d[0],
      y: d => d[1],
      // fill colour by temperature's answer-quantile bucket, using the same
      // scale as the ts plot above so the two match; z: null keeps this a
      // single contiguous area (no gaps at the colour boundaries) rather
      // than splitting into separate non-touching series per colour - see
      // https://observablehq.com/plot/marks/area#varying-color
      fill: d => tavgQuantileScale(d[0]),
      z: null,
      curve: "basis"
      }),
    // today marker
    Plot.ruleX([today.Tavg], {
      stroke: "#333333",
      strokeWidth: 2
    }),
    Plot.text([
      { text: `TODAY: ${today.Tavg.toFixed(1)}°C` }
    ], {
      x: () => today.Tavg,
      text: "text",
      frameAnchor: "top",
      lineAnchor: "middle",
      textAnchor: "end",
      rotate: 270,
      dy: 6,
      dx: -10,
      fill: "#333333",
      stroke: "#eeeeee",
      strokeWidth: 5
    }),
    // 5th/50th/95th percentile labels
    Plot.text([
      { x: tavg05, text: `5th percentile: ${tavg05.toFixed(1)}°C` },
      { x: tavg50, text: `Median: ${tavg50.toFixed(1)}°C` },
      { x: tavg95, text: `95th percentile: ${tavg95.toFixed(1)}°C` }
    ], {
      x: "x",
      text: "text",
      frameAnchor: "bottom",
      lineAnchor: "middle",
      textAnchor: "start",
      rotate: -90,
      dy: -6,
      fill: "#333333",
      stroke: "#eeeeee",
      strokeWidth: 5
    }),
  ],
  y: {
    axis: null
  },
  x: {
    tickFormat: d => `${d}°C`,
    label: "Daily average temperature",
  },
  style: {
    fontFamily: "Roboto Condensed",
    fontWeight: "bold",
    fontSize: 16
  },
  height: 320,
  marginBottom: 50,
  title: `${statsPlace.isit_label} daily average temperatures for the two weeks around ${dayMonthLabel}`,
  caption: plotCaption
})
```

# ... and the rest of the year.

We've compared every day this year at <strong> ${statsPlace.isit_label}</strong> to similar times of year in the past. Red days were hot compared to records; blue days were cold. 

```{ojs}
//| label: hw
//| classes: iihrn-figure
//| echo: false
heatmapYear = (new Date()).toLocaleString("en-US", {timeZone: "Australia/Melbourne", year: "numeric"})
heatmapData = FA(bucket_processed + stationId + "-" + heatmapYear + ".csv").csv({ typed: true })
```

```{ojs}
//| label: hw-ojs
//| classes: iihrn-figure
//| echo: false

monthOrder = ["Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr", "May", "Jun", "Jul", "Aug", "Sep", "Oct", "Nov", "Dec"]
month3 = d3.timeFormat("%b")

heatmapPrepped = heatmapData.map(d => ({
  ...d,
  month: month3(d.date),
  day: d.date.getDate()
}))

// cumulative 5%-multiples of each answer tier's `size`, eg [0,5,20,40,60,80,95,100] -
// the lambda's createHeatmapPlot() uses these same breaks (0.05,0.2,0.4,0.6,0.8,0.95)
// for its image()/colkey() call, so cell shading and legend bands line up with it
answerBreaks = answers.reduce((acc, d) => {
  acc.push(acc[acc.length - 1] + d.size * 5)
  return acc
}, [0])

percentileColorScale = d3.scaleThreshold()
  .domain(answerBreaks.slice(1, -1))
  .range(answers.map(d => d.fill1))

// contrasting text colour per tier (white on the dark blue/red extremes,
// dark grey on the light middle tiers) - reusing answers' own `color` field,
// which already exists for exactly this purpose in the answer banner above
percentileTextColorScale = d3.scaleThreshold()
  .domain(answerBreaks.slice(1, -1))
  .range(answers.map(d => d.color))


md`### ${statsPlace.isit_label} percentiles for ${heatmapYear}`

// flip the heatmap axes at narrow widths
// hide the text layer altogether at very narrow widths
heatmapIsNarrow = width < 768
heatmapIsVeryNarrow = width < 450
heatmapHeight = heatmapIsNarrow ? 2100 : 425
heatmapFontSize = heatmapIsNarrow ? 20 : 12

heatmapStyle = ({
  fontFamily: "Roboto Condensed",
  fontWeight: "bold",
  fontSize: heatmapFontSize
})

heatmapPlot = Plot.plot({
  marginLeft: 40,
  marginTop: 30,
  marginBottom: 10,
  x: heatmapIsNarrow ? {
    domain: monthOrder,
    label: null,
    axis: "top",
    tickSize: 0,
    tickFormat: d => d.charAt(0),
    padding: 0
  } : {
    domain: d3.range(1, 32),
    label: null,
    axis: "top",
    tickSize: 0,
    padding: 0
  },
  y: heatmapIsNarrow ? {
    domain: d3.range(1, 32),
    label: null,
    tickSize: 0,
    padding: 0
  } : {
    domain: monthOrder,
    label: null,
    tickSize: 0,
    padding: 0
  },
  marks: [
    Plot.cell(heatmapPrepped, {
      x: heatmapIsNarrow ? "month" : "day",
      y: heatmapIsNarrow ? "day" : "month",
      fill: d => percentileColorScale(d.percentile),
      inset: 0
    }),
    heatmapIsVeryNarrow ? null : Plot.text(heatmapPrepped, {
      x: heatmapIsNarrow ? "month" : "day",
      y: heatmapIsNarrow ? "day" : "month",
      text: d => Math.round(d.percentile),
      fill: d => percentileTextColorScale(d.percentile),
      fontSize: heatmapFontSize
    }),
    Plot.frame({ stroke: "#333333", strokeWidth: 1 })
  ],
  height: heatmapHeight,
  width: 900,
  style: heatmapStyle,
  caption: plotCaption
})

// vertical colour-bar legend: a single stacked column, one rect per answer
// tier, with height proportional to the tier's width (matching the lambda's
// colkey() bands) rather than 7 equal-height swatches - Plot's built-in
// legends don't support this (threshold color legends only render as a
// horizontal ramp), so it's built by hand from the same answerBreaks
answerBands = answers.map((d, i) => ({
  y1: answerBreaks[i],
  y2: answerBreaks[i + 1],
  fill: d.fill1
}))

heatmapLegend = Plot.plot({
  marginLeft: 6,
  marginRight: 34,
  marginTop: 30,
  marginBottom: 10,
  x: {
    axis: null,
    domain: [0, 1]
  },
  y: {
    domain: [0, 100],
    ticks: answerBreaks,
    label: null,
    axis: "right"
  },
  marks: [
    Plot.rect(answerBands, { x1: 0, x2: 1, y1: "y1", y2: "y2", fill: "fill" }),
    Plot.frame({ stroke: "#333333", strokeWidth: 1 })
  ],
  width: 80,
  height: heatmapHeight,
  marginRight: 50,
  style: heatmapStyle
})

html`<div style="display: flex; align-items: flex-start;">
  <div style="flex: 1 1 auto; min-width: 0;">${heatmapPlot}</div>
  ${heatmapLegend}
</div>`
```
